+---

+title: Run the cycle check on undeleteTask and on undo of a delete
+---
+## What
+divergence.md X7 (§1.1, §11 bugs). This is work on the Swift package (S/ = Sources/FoundationModelsKanban/).
+
+Problem: `undeleteTask` can bring back a cycle. The cycle check runs only when `dependsOn` or the body changes (S/GraphQL/TaskMutations.swift:303-305, S/GraphQL/UndoMutations.swift:289-298). `undeleteTask` calls `setDeleted` (S/GraphQL/ColumnActorMutations.swift:443-453), which does no cycle check. Example: A→B→C, then delete B, then add C→A, then undelete B. The result is the cycle A→B→C→A, with no error. This can occur in one board or across boards.
+
+Change: `undeleteTask`, and an undo (or redo) that makes a tombstoned task live again, run the same cycle check as a write of `dependsOn`. A cycle gives `DEPENDENCY_CYCLE` and writes nothing. For a cycle across boards, lock each board that the check read, as the current cross-board cycle check does.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] The example above gives `DEPENDENCY_CYCLE` on `undeleteTask(B)`, and B stays deleted.
+- [ ] Undo of the delete of B in the same state gives `DEPENDENCY_CYCLE` and writes nothing.
+- [ ] The same example across two boards gives `DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`.
+- [ ] `undeleteTask` with no cycle works as before.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] The one-board example with `undeleteTask`.
+- [ ] The one-board example with `undo` of the delete.
+- [ ] The cross-board example.
+- [ ] Tests use temporary fixture folders. Never use the `.kanban/` of this repo (it is a Rust board).
+- [ ] `swift test` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    Research done.
+    - `WorkingCopy.setDeleted` (S/GraphQL/ColumnActorMutations.swift) applies the delete patch with no cycle check. `changeDeleted` calls it for undeleteTask.
+    - `WorkingCopy.checkCycles(after:inBoard:)` (S/GraphQL/UndoMutations.swift) checks a task only when the inverse has a body change or an `add` of `dependsOn`. An inverse with `delete: false` (undo of a delete, or redo of an undo of an add) is not checked.

+    - An undo of the delete of B after C->A gives no UNDO_CONFLICT: the later patch is on C and makes no edge to B, and the inverse of B is not a tombstone.
+    Plan: in setDeleted, run checkNoCycle when a tombstoned task becomes live. In checkCycles, also check a task whose inverse has `delete == false`. Tests in a new suite with `.watcherBudget`, git repos in a GitSandbox (temporary folders).
